newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 3.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The resignation of Deputy Foreign Minister Christos Rozakis yesterday is a bad start for 1997 for the government and for Prime Minister Costas Simitis personally, serving to confirm reports of dissension between Simitis's hand-picked choice and Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos in the sensitive area of foreign policy.

--Simitis is concerned about the course of the difficult tasks ahead of the government: today's inner cabinet is expected to prioritise tasks and Simitis is expected to ask for ministers to stick to timeframes.

--The first fortnight of the year will see a further fall in bank interest rates, sources say. Banks believe that a reduction in returns from state titles following the levy of a new tax, as well as the fall in inflation, has created the margins for lower interest on deposit and lending rates.
--Athens Mayor Dimitris Avramopoulos has hinted at his intention to contest the leadership of the conservative opposition party New Democracy, but said he will serve out his term as mayor.

--Rozakis's resignation is a blow to Simitis's efforts to protray a more flexible foreign policy in the sensitive areas of Greek-Turkish relations and Cyprus. Citing ill health for his resignation, Rozakis nevertheless let loose volleys at critics who did not allow him to complete his work.
--A Greek professor at MIT expounds on his theory why the Dystos sank off the island of Evia last weekend. Port authorities have called in the lone survivor for more questioning.

--Pangalos reigns at the foreign ministry: this is the message from the Rozakis resignation. Rozakis, a close friend of Simitis, had been the target of intense criticism when he voiced opinions different to the foreign ministry's. Simitis advisers stressed, however, there would be no change in the government's foreign policy.
--Turkey's tourist boom over the past two years shows no sign of abating: tourist figures for the neighbouring country this year is expected to surpass Greek numbers.

--Thessaloniki's Macedonia Airport remain closed for the fourth day yesterday, due to heavy fog. Transport Minister Haris Kastanidis yesterday vowed to find a solution to the woes of the European Cultural Capital's airport.
--Rozakis reportedly decided to resign from "his living nightmare" at the foreign ministry after a fortnight of consultations with the prime minister.
